mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the past two months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the past month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals an increase in economic activity, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which is negative for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in the past quarter signals a weakening economy, which is a negative indicator for corporate earnings and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
